classification.difficultyReason: Compare the target age with an explicitly supplied range and apply the taught limitation of extrapolation; no equation manipulation or biological knowledge is required.

content.prompt:
Priya collected data on the age ($a$), in years, and the height ($h$), in metres, of eucalyptus trees aged 3 to 9 years. She constructed the line of best fit $h = 0.45a + 1.2$.

Why would this model not be useful for predicting the height of a 40-year-old tree?

answer.short: 40 years is far outside the observed ages of 3 to 9 years, so the prediction would be extrapolation and less reliable.
answer.worked: An age of 40 years is far outside the observed age range of 3 to 9 years, so the prediction would be extrapolation. The relationship may change beyond the known data, so the prediction would be less reliable.
